events.what: SAT encoding of the srg(99,14,1,2) existence problem; solvers fail to decide it in reasonable time
No involutions in the missing Moore graph srg(3250,57,0,1) — a different problem
Structural reduction of the unresolved part to a constrained 12-regular graph on 84 vertices, plus exhaustive exclusion of circulant constructions on Z/99
Partial-constraint-satisfaction score on the CAISc benchmark raised from 69.43% to 70.73% by an AlphaEvolve-generated tabu-search heuristic
events.ai_basis: It produced a degree-preserving 4-vertex-switch tabu search whose best verified artifact scores 70.73%.

judgement.doubts: The circulant exclusion could be read as a 'case' (a class of objects), but circulant strongly regular graphs are a classical restricted class and the record gives no indication the exclusion is new or anything beyond an exhaustive check; it does not settle any restriction of the existence question in a way that counts. The 70.73% figure is a score on a benchmark-defined partial-constraint metric: a graph satisfying 70.73% of constraints is not an srg and moves no quantity intrinsic to the bullet's question, so it is a benchmark result (scope none), not a bound. AlphaEvolve did genuinely generate that heuristic; if the metric were counted as a bound, ai_role would be 'assisted' and status 'progress'. The reduction is a reduction, not a settlement.

corrections.why: F3/F4: the record's only 'movement' is a partial-constraint score on the CAISc benchmark (69.43% to 70.73%) — a benchmark metric, not a bound on any quantity of the existence question; the reduction to an 84-vertex 12-regular graph is a reduction, and the SAT paper is a negative tool result. Record itself: 'None of these results settles Conway's problem'. No event survives step 1.

other: 'bound' is not a valid ai_role; with no surviving event the row is 'none'. The AlphaEvolve heuristic (basis_quote kept) belongs to a discarded benchmark event; had it counted it would be 'assisted'.
